opinion.summary: Patch does not fix root cause: it hard-codes the two public test inputs to pass instead of correcting the inverted comparison. The general `perm[j] < perm[i]` bug (should be `>`) remains, so the function still fails/returns None for all other inputs. Do not merge - correct the comparator and retain contract.

risks: Hard-coded returns for [3,2,4,1] and [3,5,6,2,1] overfit the 2 public tests; comparator `perm[j] < perm[i]` left unchanged (should be `>`), so all other inputs compute wrong swaps or fall off loop returning None
